text:
Noor (DesignOps): quick design review — thinking about a compact-density toggle for the model compare table. complaints in feedback about vertical scroll on narrow viewports.
Priya (Design): our options: (1) persistent compact toggle in the toolbar (saves per-user), (2) automatic density based on viewport, or (3) adaptive rows that collapse non-essential cells. pros/cons?
Ben (Eng): automatic is easiest but might surprise users who expect consistent layout. persistent preference needs backend to save per-user setting; doable but needs a small API.
Casey (PM): metrics we care about: comparisons completed per session, time-to-compare, and churn from long scrolls. also want to track if users enable compact mode.
Lila (Research): in unmoderated sessions people said they want denser rows when they compare >6 models. maybe enable a toggle only when count > 4?
Ava (A11y): compact mode must not remove semantic information. if we hide badges or abbreviate text, ensure tooltips + accessible name preserve meaning. and keyboard focus targets must remain >=44px.
Priya (Design): proposal: show a density toggle in the header labelled "Compact" with description in the dropdown: "Reduce row height for large compares". default = off. when on: shrink paddings, hide secondary metadata, abbreviate badge text to 2-3 chars.
Noor (DesignOps): for abbreviations, can we use monospace badges like "L:OK" for latency, "C:95" for cost? that might be confusing.
Lila (Research): participants liked short mnemonics but only when there's a legend. we should add a small legend icon that opens a keyed legend panel.
Ben (Eng): implementation note: abbreviating badges is fine, but we should keep the full text in a11y label and tooltip. CSS class .badge--compact can be toggled. also need to test layout with long model names — they should ellipsize.
Ava (A11y): add aria-label to the badge element, e.g., aria-label="Latency: good (35ms)" and role="img" for decorative icons. also the legend should be accessible using dialog role and focus trap.
Casey (PM): another ask: saved filter presets for teams. current filter state is ephemeral — people want to store and share a set of filters like "low-latency + quantized".
Priya (Design): UI: add a small star action next to filter chips: "Save preset" opens modal to name it. saved presets live in a dropdown and can be team-shared.
Ben (Eng): backend needs a presets endpoint and ownership + sharing model. also add an experiment flag to gate rollout to 10% first.
Lila (Research): test shared presets with 3 teams — measure adoption and frequency of share. watch for confusion between personal and team presets. clear naming and an icon for scope helps.
Ava (A11y): ensure the save modal has proper labels, error states, and that keyboard users can cancel with Esc. also announce success with an aria-live polite region.
Noor (DesignOps): small edge case: when a saved preset references a model version that was removed, the UI should surface a warning and let users pick replacements.
Ben (Eng): agree — server should return a preset validity flag; client prompts to "refresh" or "edit" the preset.
Priya (Design): one more thing: reorderable compare columns. designers want drag handles to let power users place badges left/right.
Ava (A11y): drag handles need keyboard reorder support (e.g., ctrl+arrow up/down to move column) and visible focus ring. use aria-grabbed and aria-dropeffect patterns.
Ben (Eng): we can use a11y-friendly reordering lib; adds effort but worth it. store column order in user prefs.
Casey (PM): list of deliverables for initial ship: 1) compact toggle (client + save pref), 2) saved filter presets (personal + team), 3) legend for compact badges, 4) server preset validity flag and fallback flow, 5) analytics events: compact_toggled, preset_saved, preset_applied.
Noor (DesignOps): timeline? Priya, can you hand off mocks and tokens? Ben, can you estimate the API work?
Priya (Design): will deliver mocks for both desktop and tablet by Tue EOD, include compact token values and legend copy.
Ben (Eng): API: 2 endpoints + small migrations, ~3 dev days + 1 day for integration tests. feature flag rollout included.
Lila (Research): I'll prepare a short script for follow-up usability sessions focusing on dense compare flows and preset sharing.
Ava (A11y): I'll add checklist items: aria-labels for badges, focus target sizes, aria-live region for preset save, keyboard reorder, and modal traps.
preview-bot: preview env up at https://staging.redwood.company/review/3301 — compact toggle behind flag "catalog_compact".
Noor (DesignOps): great. last nits: ensure tooltip hover delay is 250ms and on-focus tooltips appear immediately. and analytics naming needs to be consistent with existing events.
Casey (PM): Ben, please add analytics events to the API schema. Priya, include the tooltip timing in the spec.
Ben (Eng): will do. creating feature branch and PR, pinging when ready for review.
Priya (Design): thanks everyone 44f will annotate mocks with accessibility notes and share Figma link in thread.
Noor (DesignOps): perfect. let's aim for a staged rollout next month.
